questionText:
Let $z = 1 + i\sqrt{3}$.

(a) Express $z$ in polar form $r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$.
(b) Using De Moivre's Theorem, find $z^6$. Give your answer as a real or complex number in the form $a + bi$.
markingScheme:
(a) Compute modulus $|z| = 2$ **(1 mark)**
(a) Compute argument $\arg z = \pi/3$ **(1 mark)**
(a) Write polar form $2(\cos(\pi/3) + i\sin(\pi/3))$ **(1 mark)**
(b) State De Moivre: $z^n = r^n(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)$ **(1 mark)**
(b) Apply with $n = 6$: $2^6(\cos 2\pi + i\sin 2\pi)$ **(1 mark)**
(b) Simplify to $64$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.explanation: $z = 1 + i\sqrt{3}$ is in the first quadrant. $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1} = \sqrt{3}$, so $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
